title: Events and Background in a Story

sections.title: Two jobs for two tenses
sections.content: You know the *indefinido* from A2 Unit 11, the *imperfecto* from A2 Unit 21 and the contrast between them from A2 Unit 22. At B2 that contrast becomes a storytelling tool. The *indefinido* looks at an action as finished, a closed block, so a chain of *indefinido* verbs forms the plot: first this happened, then that. The *imperfecto* looks at an action from the inside, with no start or end in view, so it suits whatever was already there when the events happened: the time, the weather, a feeling, what someone was doing. Take the *imperfecto* lines out of a story and the plot still moves, but it feels bare.

sections.title: Plot and scenery
rows: Llegó, abrió la carta y se sentó.
Indefinido: three events, one after the other. Each one pushes the plot forward.
Era de noche y llovía mucho.
Imperfecto: the time and the weather. Nothing happens; the scene is set.
Estaba cansado y no tenía hambre.
Imperfecto: how someone felt. It is a state, not an event.
Both together: an action in progress (imperfecto) and the event that breaks into it (indefinido).

items.spanish: Llovía cuando salimos de la estación.
items.english: It was raining when we left the station.

items.spanish: Era de noche y hacía frío cuando llegó el tren.
items.english: It was night and it was cold when the train arrived.

items.spanish: Mientras todos dormían, ella escribió una carta.
items.english: While everyone was asleep, she wrote a letter.

items.spanish: Estaba cansada, pero abrió la puerta y entró.
items.english: She was tired, but she opened the door and went in.

sections.content: A quick test: if the next question could be "and then what happened?", use the *indefinido*. If it could be "what was it like?" or "what was going on?", use the *imperfecto*. A scene can have several *imperfecto* verbs in a row and then one *indefinido* verb that breaks in.
